hints: Focus on which substances actually appear in the Kp expression, remember Kp only uses gases.
Write the Kp expression for this reaction, you should have two partial pressures on top and one on the bottom.
Now put Pa in place of each partial pressure and cancel top and bottom to leave the final unit.
walkthrough:
**Write the Kp expression correctly**

Remember Kp uses partial pressures of gases only. Solids are left out completely.

$$K_p = \frac{p(\text{H}_2) \times p(\text{CO})}{p(\text{H}_2\text{O})}$$

**Put in the units for pressure**

Each partial pressure, $p$, is measured in pascals, $\text{Pa}$. So substitute Pa for every $p$ term.

$$\text{units of } K_p = \frac{\text{Pa} \times \text{Pa}}{\text{Pa}}$$

**Simplify to find the final unit**

Two Pa units on top and one on the bottom cancel to leave just one Pa.

$$\text{units of } K_p = \text{Pa}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Pa}^{-1}$ would mean more pressure units on the bottom than the top, like 1 gas product and 2 gas reactants. Here we have 2 gas products and only 1 gas reactant.
options.B: Correct. With $\text{C(s)}$ omitted, $K_p = p(\text{H}_2)p(\text{CO})/p(\text{H}_2\text{O})$, so units are $(\text{Pa} \times \text{Pa})/\text{Pa} = \text{Pa}$.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{Pa}^2$ would come from forgetting to divide by $p(\text{H}_2\text{O})$, or from wrongly including $\text{C(s)}$ as a bottom term that has no units to cancel. You must divide by the reactant gas.
options.D: Incorrect. Kp has no units only when the number of gaseous moles is the same on both sides so all Pa units cancel. Here 2 gas moles form from 1 gas mole, so one Pa unit is left over.
